+// "On its own" is one condition with two independent reasons, and they are
+// separate questions because they cost different things:

+//   - `needsReservedFlag` — the group holds fuzzing documents, and `-dast` on a
+//     directory without one aborts the whole invocation, so the flag needs an
+//     invocation that contains nothing else. The FLAG is the reason.
+//   - `runsAlone` — the group is a single document the plan gave a batch of its
+//     own because it declares no deadline of its own. The DEADLINE is the
+//     reason, and no flag is involved.

+// 131 documents, 8 invocations at exit 1 and zero records between them.

+	return c.runsAlone() || c.needsReservedFlag()
+}
+
+// needsReservedFlag reports whether this group's own documents declare the
+// capability whose flag must not share an invocation with other protocols.
+//
+// It reads the capability list only — never the marker. A document that never
+// asked for the flag cannot be given it, because the flag is not what isolates

 		}

+// reason other than the reserved flag — a document that can block forever, or a
+// set of same-id documents the binary would otherwise load only one of.
+//
+// A key built by appending a marker to a capability list is exactly this shape,
+// so "the key carries more tokens than it has capabilities" is the test.
+func (c capabilityKey) runsAlone() bool {
+	return len(c.parts()) > len(c.parseCapabilities())
+}

+// fuzzingTemplate declares the reserved capability the flag exists for: a
+// `payloads:` block that names its `fuzzing:` engine. nuclei loads such a document
+// only under `-dast`, and it refuses an invocation that carries `-dast` while
+// holding no such document, which is why the flag needs a batch of its own.
+const fuzzingTemplate = `id: rr-fuzzing-probe
+info:
+  name: rr fuzzing probe
+  author: rr
+  severity: info
+http:
+  - method: GET
+    path:
+      - "{{BaseURL}}/probe"
+    payloads:
+      value:
+        - one
+    fuzzing:
+      - type: replace
+        method: GET
+    matchers:
+      - type: word
+        words:
+          - never
+`
+
+// stagingTemplateWithCapabilities parses a document and asserts the capability set
+// it declares, so a test that depends on the flag cannot pass because the parser
+// stopped reading the declaration.
+func stagingTemplateWithCapabilities(t *testing.T, name, body string, want []Capability) StagedFile {
+	t.Helper()
+	meta, reason := parseTemplateDocument(body)
+	if reason != "" {
+		t.Fatalf("parse %s: %s", name, reason)
+	}
+	got := map[Capability]bool{}
+	for _, capability := range meta.Capabilities {
+		got[capability] = true
+	}
+	for _, capability := range want {
+		if !got[capability] {
+			t.Fatalf("%s: the parser does not report %q, so this test would pass "+
+				"for the wrong reason. Capabilities read: %v", name, capability, meta.Capabilities)
+		}
+	}
+	return StagedFile{UploadName: name, Meta: meta}
+}
+
+// nucleiCorpusFolder finds the official corpus's `javascript` folder, which is
+// where the eight lost verdicts came from. It is not required: the rest of this
+// file runs without it.

+	t.Helper()
+	for _, root := range []string{
+		filepath.Join("/home/kali/.local/nuclei-templates"),
+		filepath.Join("..", "nuclei-templates"),
+	} {
+		candidate := filepath.Join(root, "javascript")
+		if info, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
+			return candidate
+		}
+	}
+	return ""
+}

"""Firefox-прогон сценарію оператора: завантаження папки шаблонів і запуск.

Тільки реальний браузер, як вимагає власник: Firefox + справжній вибір папки
(`webkitdirectory`), а не виклик API. Захоплюється console, network і стан
прогресу, щоб побачити, де саме зупиняється.
"""

import json
import sys
import time

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
CORPUS = "/home/kali/Desktop/DevBackUp-vecher07101/nuclei-templates/javascript"
WATCH_SECONDS = 150


def main() -> int:
    console = []
    requests = []
    failures = []

    with sync_playwright() as play:
        browser = play.firefox.launch(headless=True)
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1356, "height": 652})

        page.on("console", lambda msg: console.append(f"[{msg.type}] {msg.text}"))
        page.on("pageerror", lambda err: console.append(f"[pageerror] {err}"))
        page.on(
            "requestfailed",
            lambda req: failures.append(f"{req.method} {req.url} -> {req.failure}"),
        )

        def on_response(res):
            if "/api/scanner/nuclei/" in res.url:
                requests.append(
                    {"t": round(time.time() - start, 2), "url": res.url,
                     "status": res.status, "method": res.request.method}
                )

        start = time.time()
        page.on("response", on_response)

        page.goto(BASE + "/", wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=60_000)
        print("page loaded, title:", page.title())

        # Відкриваємо вкладку Scanner.
        page.get_by_role("button", name="Scanner", exact=True).first.click()
        page.wait_for_timeout(800)
        print("scanner view:", page.get_attribute("#scanner", "class") if page.query_selector("#scanner") else "?")

        # Nuclei scan view.
        page.get_by_role("button", name="Nuclei scan").first.click()
        page.wait_for_timeout(500)

        # Ціль.
        page.fill("#scanner-url", "https://yandex.ru")

        # Справжній вибір папки: webkitdirectory.
        print("uploading folder via the real file input...")
        page.set_input_files("#scanner-yaml-dir", CORPUS)
        page.wait_for_timeout(3000)
        chips = page.query_selector_all("#scanner-files-list .file-chip")
        print("folder chips in the UI:", len(chips))
        if chips:
            print("first chip:", (chips[0].inner_text() or "").strip())

        # Категорія + запуск.
        print("clicking Run templates...")
        page.click("#scanner-templates-run")

        # Спостерігаємо, що саме зависає.
        deadline = time.time() + WATCH_SECONDS
        last = None
        while time.time() < deadline:
            label = page.inner_text("#scanner-upload-progress") if page.query_selector("#scanner-upload-progress") else ""
            status = page.inner_text("#scanner-status") if page.query_selector("#scanner-status") else ""
            state = page.get_attribute("[data-report-state]", "data-report-state") if page.query_selector("[data-report-state]") else ""
            snapshot = (label.strip(), status.strip(), state)
            if snapshot != last:
                print("t=%5.1fs label=%r status=%r state=%r" % (
                    time.time() - start, snapshot[0][:70], snapshot[1][:70], snapshot[2]))
                last = snapshot
            if state in ("completed", "failed", "cancelled"):
                break
            page.wait_for_timeout(2000)

        print("\n=== network (scanner endpoints) ===")
        for item in requests:
            print("  t=%6.2fs %-6s %s -> %s" % (item["t"], item["method"], item["url"], item["status"]))
        print("\n=== console ===")
        for line in console[-40:]:
            print("  " + line)
        if failures:
            print("\n=== failed requests ===")
            for line in failures:
                print("  " + line)
        page.screenshot(path="/tmp/opencode/firefox-upload.png", full_page=False)
        browser.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

So the task: when the operator presses Cancel, the SSE stream must be closed, so the connection is released.

Currently the cancel handler:
1. sets `scannerRun.cancelling = true`
2. disables the button
3. POSTs /cancel
4. On success: does NOTHING more — relies on the stream's `done` event to end the run and call `finish()` → `source.close()`.

If the job never terminates (or the stream stalls), the SSE connection is held indefinitely, and with Firefox/Chromium's 6-connection-per-host limit, the next upload fetch queues forever → exactly the observed symptom.

Fix: after a successful cancel POST, close the SSE stream locally and settle the run — the job is cancelled server-side, so the client doesn't need to keep the stream open. But we must still let the final report/state be coherent.

Careful design:
- On successful cancel: call `source.close()`, stop the ticker, and resolve the promise with the cancelled state so the UI settles (no dangling promise).
- But the authoritative terminal state comes from the job. After cancelling, we could do one final GET of the job snapshot to render the final report. That's honest: the server is the authority.

Now I understand the structure. The fix:

On a **successful** cancel POST, the client must:
1. Close the SSE stream immediately (release the connection).
2. Settle the run so the promise doesn't dangle and the UI shows the cancelled state.
3. Not lose the final report — but for a cancelled run there IS no final report (the job returns `cancelled` with `run=nil`, per `job.finish(JobCancelled, nil, runErr)`).

So the honest behaviour: after a successful cancel, close the stream, settle as cancelled, and do one final GET of the job snapshot to render whatever the server recorded (which for a cancelled run is `state: cancelled`).

Let me look at what the current `finish` does for cancelled: `setScanProgress({phase:'cancelled', ...})`, status text, `onError(error)`, `reject(error)`. And `runScannerTemplates` catches and does nothing extra.

So the fix in the cancel handler:
```js
const cancelled = await readJSON(await fetch(`.../cancel`, {method:'POST'}));
// The server accepted the cancellation: the run is over from here on. The
// stream is closed now rather than left to end on its own, because ...
if (scannerRun?.source) { ... }
```

But `finish` is a closure inside `followScannerJob` — the cancel handler can't reach it. I need a way for the cancel handler to settle the run.

Options:
a) Expose a settle function on `scannerRun`, e.g. `scannerRun.settle = finish`.
b) In the cancel handler, call `stopScanTicker()` (which closes `scannerRun.source`), then set the UI state to cancelled and re-enable the button.

Option (b) is simpler and doesn't require exposing internals. But then the promise from `followScannerJob` never settles — it's awaited by `runScannerTemplates` in a try/finally, so `finally` would never run, leaving `$('scanner-templates-run').disabled = true` forever. That's a real bug: the Run button would stay disabled.

So I need the promise to settle. Best: have `followScannerJob` return an object with a `cancel`-aware settle, or expose the settle function.

Cleanest minimal change: store the settle function on `scannerRun` so the cancel handler can call it.

- In `followScannerJob`, after defining `finish`, set `scannerRun.settle = finish;`
- In `stopScanTicker()` or after settle, clear `scannerRun.settle = null`.
- In the cancel handler, on success: fetch the final job state (authoritative), then call `scannerRun.settle?.(...)` with a cancelled error.

Wait — but there's a subtlety. If the job actually finished successfully just before the cancel, we should show completed, not cancelled. The cancel response tells us: `CancelNucleiJob` returns 404/409 if already finished. Let me check the engine endpoint's response for an already-finished job.

Let me check the engine's cancel handler.

BUT: `executeBatch` waits on `command.Wait()` with `WaitDelay 2s`; the nuclei process gets SIGKILLed via process group. Then batches continue... Actually `for _, batch := range plan.Batches { outcome, err := executeBatch(...) }` — on ctx cancel it returns early with ctxErr. So it should end within seconds.

Hmm, so why would the stream linger? Unless... `applyLocalFallback` runs with the cancelled ctx — the pool returns quickly since ctx is done. OK.

So the leak isn't necessarily infinite. But there IS a real window: between the Cancel click and the `done` frame, the SSE stays open. If the operator then clicks "Run templates" again immediately, a new upload must be sent — and the old stream is still occupying 1 connection. With several such runs, connections accumulate.

Also the operator's own log shows: job cancelled at 23:31:18, and the stream GET logged at 23:31:20 — so it did end 2s later. So not infinite.

TARGET = os.environ.get("TARGET", "https://yandex.ru")


def panel(page):
    phase = page.inner_text("#scanner-progress-phase") if page.query_selector("#scanner-progress-phase") else ""
    stats = page.inner_text("#scanner-progress-stats") if page.query_selector("#scanner-progress-stats") else ""
    status = page.inner_text("#scanner-status") if page.query_selector("#scanner-status") else ""
    return phase.strip(), stats.strip(), status.strip()


def upload_and_run(page, start):
    page.click("#scanner-templates-run")
    # Панель після завантаження: напис про завантаження зник, лічильник реальний.
    seen = None
    deadline = time.time() + 90
    while time.time() < deadline:
        phase, stats, status = panel(page)
        if (phase, stats, status) != seen:
            print("  t=%5.1fs phase=%r stats=%r status=%r" % (
                time.time() - start, phase[:46], stats[:28], status[:46]))
            seen = (phase, stats, status)
        if "Uploading" not in phase and "Завантаження" not in phase:
            return True
        page.wait_for_timeout(700)
    return False


def main() -> int:
    console = []
    events = []
    start = time.time()

    with sync_playwright() as play:
        browser = play.firefox.launch(headless=True)
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1356, "height": 652})
        page.on("console", lambda m: console.append(f"[{m.type}] {m.text}"))
        page.on("pageerror", lambda e: console.append(f"[pageerror] {e}"))
        page.on("response", lambda r: events.append(

             r.url.replace(BASE, ""), r.status)
        ) if "/api/scanner/nuclei/" in r.url else None)

        page.goto(BASE + "/", wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=60_000)
        page.click('nav [data-tab="scanner"]')
        page.wait_for_timeout(500)
        page.click("#scanner-view-nuclei")
        page.wait_for_timeout(400)
        page.fill("#scanner-url", TARGET)
        page.set_input_files("#scanner-yaml-dir", CORPUS)
        page.wait_for_timeout(2500)
        print("folder chip:", (page.inner_text("#scanner-files-list .file-chip") or "").strip().split("\n")[0])

        print("\n== run 1 ==")
        ok = upload_and_run(page, start)
        print("  upload label cleared:", ok)
        phase, stats, status = panel(page)
        print("  panel now:", repr(phase), repr(stats))

        print("\n== Cancel ==")
        cancel = page.query_selector("#scanner-progress-cancel")
        print("  cancel visible:", cancel.is_visible() if cancel else None)
        if cancel and cancel.is_visible():
            cancel.click()
            page.wait_for_timeout(3000)
        phase, stats, status = panel(page)
        print("  after cancel:", repr(phase), repr(stats), repr(status))
        # SSE мав закритися: у браузері більше не має бути відкритого джерела.
        print("  scannerRun.source:", page.evaluate(
            "() => (window.scannerRun && window.scannerRun.source) ? 'open' : 'null'"))
        print("  run button enabled:", page.is_enabled("#scanner-templates-run"))

        print("\n== run 2 (the one that used to hang) ==")
        t2 = time.time()
        ok2 = upload_and_run(page, start)
        print("  upload label cleared:", ok2)
        phase, stats, status = panel(page)
        print("  panel now:", repr(phase), repr(stats))
        print("  seconds from click to a cleared label: %.1f" % (time.time() - t2))

        print("\n== network ==")
        for t, method, url, code in events:
            print("  t=%6.2fs %-6s %-62s %s" % (t, method, url, code))
        print("\n== console ==")
        for line in console[-15:]:
            print("  " + line)
        page.screenshot(path="/tmp/opencode/firefox-cancel-fix.png")
        browser.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def scanner_nuclei_job_stream(request, job_id):
    """Proxy the engine's live scan stream without buffering individual lines.

    A folder scan streams one event per finished template, so results reach the
    browser while nuclei is still working instead of arriving all at once.

    The read deadline is the same one the passive traffic stream uses, and for
    the same reason. A paused scan writes no events at all, and a single slow
    template can go a long time without one, so a stream that only produced
    bytes on real progress looked dead to its own read deadline: the read raised
    `TimeoutError`, the proxy died, and the browser reported a transport failure
    for a job that was still running. Resuming the run then failed against a
    stream nobody was listening to any more. A bounded read with a keepalive
    comment keeps a quiet run connected, and an overall lifetime still lets the
    client reconnect with its cursor.
    """
    if request.method != "GET":
        return JsonResponse({"error": "method not allowed"}, status=405)
    cursor = request.headers.get("Last-Event-ID") or request.GET.get("last_event_id", "")

So nuclei traffic DOES get a capture context (`tool_run_route(request, "nuclei", url)`) → proxy header → so it should be linked and appear in History.

import sys
import time

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
CORPUS = "/home/kali/Desktop/DevBackUp-vecher07101/nuclei-templates/javascript"


def history_rows(page):

    with sync_playwright() as play:

messages.summary:
## Objective
Fix bugs in the Request-Rider Nuclei scanner: templates "don't load / don't start" via the UI, and the scan appears to hang. Continue the work started in previous sessions (`session-ses_eece.md` tasks NUCLEI-JOB-HANG, NUCLEI-JAVASCRIPT-REPORT, NUCLEI-CODE-FLAG).

## Requirements
- **User instruction:** "делать тесты только через реальное открытие фаерфокс и загрузки папки" — all UI verification must go through real Firefox with a real folder upload (`webkitdirectory`), not API calls.
- User supplied canonical per-folder launch commands as the contract (`code`→`-code`, `cloud`→`-code -esc -as`, `dast`→`-dast`, `file`→`-file`, `headless`→`-headless`; `dns`/`helpers`/`http`/`javascript`/`network`/`ssl` get no extra flag; always `-esc`).
- User directive: "Cancel не закриває SSE — він чекає завершення job, нужно исправить это!" — Cancel must release the SSE itself.
- Do not touch other sessions' files; `zz_dbg_test.go` in `engine/pkg/scanner/` is someone else's (dated 10-07).
- User clarified their own `cancel` calls in the log were manual, not part of the bug.

## Decisions
- Root-caused the "hang" by measurement rather than assumption; corrected my own earlier wrong conclusion (a 79 s vs 364 s comparison was invalid because it compared against a closed port).
- Fixed the capability/isolation conflation by splitting one predicate into two (`needsReservedFlag` vs `runsAlone`) instead of removing `-dast` behaviour.
- Did not add any timeout/cap to work around the SMB stall — not yet resolved.

## Work State

### Completed
- **D5 — `-dast` given to 8 documents that never asked for it.** `groupByCapability` encoded deadline-isolation as capability key `dast+<template-id>`; `executeBatch` read the first token as a capability. Measured on the real binary: `nuclei -t <copy> -esc -nss` → `Templates loaded for current scan: 1`; with `-dast` → `[FTL] Could not run nuclei: no templates provided for scan`. Before the fix, 8 of `javascript/`'s 131 documents ran as 8 invocations, all exit 1, zero records. Fixed in `nuclei_document.go` (`parts`, `parseCapabilities`, `needsReservedFlag`, `runsAlone`), `nuclei_plan.go`, `nuclei_exec.go`; new test file `nuclei_isolation_flag_test.go` (7 tests, uses a real corpus document + real binary).
- **D1 — SSE frames had no terminator.** `web/lab/views.py` `scanner_nuclei_job_stream` swallowed the blank line (`if chunk.strip(): yield chunk`). Measured: 1 frame / 23 670 bytes before → **73 frames** after. Firefox: 0 events → 100 events (`template: 58, progress: 42`), panel `Preparing` → `Scanning`. Correct sibling pattern is `traffic_stream` (`else: yield chunk`).
- **D2 — panel frozen on "Uploading 0 of 131 · request 1 of 1".** `setScanProgress` ran inside the upload loop *before* each fetch and never after; with one chunk it was the only write. Also the status line kept "Uploading templates…". Fixed both.
- **D3 — Cancel did not release the SSE.** Added `releaseScannerRunStream()`, published `scannerRun.settle = finish`, Cancel closes the stream on `200 {"state":"cancelled"}`, and `runScannerTemplates` releases the previous run **before** the first upload. Firefox: after Cancel `phase='Cancelled'`, Run button enabled, stream `closed: true`.
- **D4 — History never refreshed during a Nuclei run.** Data does arrive (API `total` 603→631 in 30 s). Added `refreshHistoryDuringScan()` with a 4 s throttle, only when the History tab is active. Firefox: 14 history GETs during the scan (was 0); newest rows confirmed `proxy | https://yandex.ru/api/about`.

### Active
- **D6 (just reported by user, unstarted):** "после обновления странички вообще все пропало и получается процес завис а его даже не вижу" — after a page reload during a running scan, everything disappears and the still-running nuclei process is invisible in the UI. Likely the missing job-restore path across reload.
- **Stall at ~62%** — not yet fixed. Measured on the live process (`ss -tnp`, pid 243268, elapsed 4:49): nuclei holds `5.255.255.77:445` and `5.255.255.77:80`. SMB templates (`javascript/misconfiguration/smb/*`, `javascript/default-logins/smb-*`) use `nuclei/smb`; yandex.ru accepts TCP/445 but never speaks SMB. `RPS` drops to 2.
- Reference run still executing in background (`setsid`, started 17:46, 1500 s timeout): the operator's own command `nuclei -duc -nc -target https://yandex.ru -t javascript -esc -o /tmp/opencode/term-js.txt` on the same corpus, log `/tmp/opencode/term-js.log` — to determine whether the stall is nuclei itself.

### Blocked
- Whether the 62% SMB stall is our bug or binary behaviour — pending the terminal reference run.

## Next Move
1. Check `/tmp/opencode/term-js.log` for the reference run's total duration and whether it completes; this settles whether the 62% stall is ours.
2. Reproduce D6 in Firefox: start a scan, reload the page mid-run, and check whether the job id is restored (`scannerRun.jobId` is module-scope and is not on `window`) and whether the stream is re-attached.
3. Add a reload-restoration path for a running Nuclei job (persist `jobId`, re-attach the SSE with `Last-Event-ID`/cursor) so a running scan survives a page reload.
4. Decide the SMB stall fix without adding a hidden cap (a visible, overridable bound is acceptable; a silent cap is not).
5. Record results in `DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md` and append claim rows to `SESSION-CLAIMS.md` (both currently unmodified by me; neighbour session `ses_integrations_20261008` touched them at 16:17/16:25).

## Relevant Files
- `web/lab/views.py`: `scanner_nuclei_job_stream` (D1 fix, ~line 3916), `scanner_nuclei_upload` (JSON, not multipart), `_nuclei_file_payload`, `scanner_nuclei_job_action` (cancel contract: 200 `{"state":"cancelled"}`, 404 `UNKNOWN_JOB`, 400 `INVALID_JOB_STATE`)
- `web/templates/lab/index.html`: `stopScanTicker`, `releaseScannerRunStream`, `followScannerJob`, `runScannerTemplates`, `refreshHistoryDuringScan`, `scannerCancel` handler (~9588), `scannerRun.settle`
- `engine/pkg/scanner/nuclei_document.go`: `parts`, `parseCapabilities`, `isolated`, `needsReservedFlag`, `runsAlone`, `capabilityFlagArgs`, `javascriptAddressesTarget`
- `engine/pkg/scanner/nuclei_plan.go`: `groupByCapability`, `materialiseBatch`, `Describe` batch_detail
- `engine/pkg/scanner/nuclei_exec.go`: `executeBatch` (line ~1091 flag decision), `buildNucleiArgs`, `RunNucleiPlan`
- `engine/pkg/scanner/nuclei_isolation_flag_test.go`: new regression tests for D5
- `engine/pkg/scanner/nuclei_jobs.go`: `NucleiJob`, `startNucleiJob`, `CancelNucleiJob`, `job.finish`
- `engine/pkg/scanner/nuclei_events.go`: `appendEvent`, `SubscribeSince`, `EventsSince`
- `engine/pkg/scanner/nuclei_progress.go`: `parseJSONStatsLine`, `newNucleiOutput`
- `engine/main.go`: `scannerNucleiJobStream` (~1641), `scannerNucleiJobAction`
- `/tmp/opencode/firefox_sse_probe.py`: SSE event capture (proved D1)
- `/tmp/opencode/backlog_probe.py`: frame-count before/after proof (1 → 73)
- `/tmp/opencode/term-js.log`: pending reference run
- `/home/kali/Desktop/DevBackUp-vecher07101/Прочее/Cесии/session-nuclei-hang-20261008.md`: my session file with all measurements

## Important Context
- Working dir is `/home/kali/Desktop/DevBackUp-vecher07101` (not a git repo). Files are being reorganised into `Прочее/` by the operator; my session file lives at `Прочее/Cесии/`.
- Template cache: `DEBUG` is off by default, so `index.html` changes need a Django restart — but `runserver` autoreload picked up `views.py` automatically and the fixes were verified live.
- Working `node --check` recipe for inline JS (from `start.sh:check_inline_js`): take the first `^<script\b[^>]*>` without `src=`, close at the first `^</script>`; the naive regex recipe fails (documented in AGENTS.md).
- Verified green: `go build ./...` rc=0, `go vet ./...` rc=0, `go test ./pkg/scanner/ -count=1` ok 77.410s, `-race` ok 90.489s, `go test ./...` rc=0, `py_compile web/lab/views.py` rc=0, `node --check` rc=0.
- Firefox folder-upload baselines (both succeed in a clean session): `javascript` 131 files → upload 200 in 2.2 s; `http` 11 666 files → 26 chunks, all 200, in 19 s. So neither folder size nor the upload code causes the hang.
- `/health` returns 404 on Django `:8000` every 30 s while engine `:8081` and worker `:8090` both answer 200 — something polls the wrong port; noted, not fixed.
- Repo corpus `nuclei-templates/` (31 MB) is in the project root; `~/.local/nuclei-templates` also exists.
- Isolate my own test runs: separate DB `requestrider_iso_20261008` was created on the shared cluster at `127.0.0.1:55433`; `/tmp/opencode/rr-engine-iso` binary built.

"""HTTP client for the Go engine gateway."""

import hashlib
import json
import logging
import re
import socket
import time
from http.client import RemoteDisconnected
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# A gateway request thread must never park forever on an engine socket. Without
# an explicit timeout, `urlopen` leaves the socket blocking, so a wedged engine
# handler pins the thread and its connection until the process exits. Every
# engine endpoint the gateway uses either answers immediately or returns a job
# handle, so a generous-but-finite default is safe.
#
# This is a transport deadline for the local gateway->engine hop, not an
# application execution budget: no job, request or target is rejected or capped
# because of it.
DEFAULT_ENGINE_TIMEOUT = 120.0

# Streaming endpoints must not be cut off mid-flight by the same deadline, so
# callers that hold a connection open pass their own value.
STREAM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 15.0


ENGINE_RAW_RESPONSE_LIMIT = 512


# Headers for every internal service call — the engine and the browser worker.
#
# `Host` is loopback on purpose. Both servers reject a request whose `Host` is
# anything else, as a DNS-rebinding guard against a page the analyst happens to
# have open (`engine/internal_auth.go:66`, `browser-worker/worker.py:2041`), and
# they answer 403 FORBIDDEN_HOST before they look at anything else. Under Docker
# the gateway addresses them by service name — `ENGINE_URL=http://engine:8081` —
# so `urllib` sends `Host: engine:8081` and every internal call is refused. The
# native stand never hit it because its `ENGINE_URL` is already
# `http://127.0.0.1:8081`, so the header sent here is byte-for-byte the one
# `urllib` sends anyway: a no-op locally, and the difference between working and
# 403 in a container.
#
# The value is deliberately bare (`127.0.0.1`, no port). The Go side splits the
# authority and falls back to the whole string when there is no port; the Python
# side truncates at the colon. Both accept it, so one value serves both without

+def health(request):
+    """Liveness of the gateway itself, with the state of the services behind it.
+
+    Every service in the stack answers `/health`, and Django was the only one that
+    did not: the route map had no such entry, so a monitor probing all four on one
+    port list got `404 Not Found` from Django forever, logged every few seconds,
+    and never said anything about the services it was meant to check. The engine
+    (`engine/main.go:1087`) and the browser worker already publish theirs.
+
+    The gateway's own answer is `200` whenever this view runs — a non-200 would
+    mean the process cannot serve at all, and the HTTP status is the signal, so
+    duplicating it in the body would be decoration. What a reader cannot otherwise
+    learn is whether the two Go/Python services behind the gateway are reachable,
+    and that is what the body carries.
+
+    Reachability is reported, not asserted: each service is asked with a short
+    deadline, and a service that does not answer is reported `unavailable` with
+    the reason rather than being folded into a single boolean. Collapsing them
+    would repeat the failure this view exists to remove — a caller told "not
+    healthy" cannot tell which service to restart.
+
+    The probes are bounded by `HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT`, not by the general engine
+    timeout: this is polled continuously, so it must stay cheap and must not
+    inherit a 120-second deadline. Both services answer immediately by design, so
+    a probe that has to wait is a probe that found a problem, and the deadline is
+    how long to wait before saying so.
+
+    The PostgreSQL round trip is the one database check worth doing here: History,
+    Traffic and every workflow read it, so a gateway serving 200 while the cluster
+    is gone would report the opposite of the truth an operator is asking for.
+    """
+    if request.method != "GET":
+        return JsonResponse({"error": "method not allowed"}, status=405)
+
+    services = {}
+
+    engine_status, engine_payload = _probe_internal_service(ENGINE_URL, "/health")
+    services["engine"] = {

+        "status": engine_status,

+    services["browser_worker"] = {

+        "status": worker_status,

+        # runtimes this installation actually has.

class GatewayHealthTests(TestCase):
    """`/health` has to exist, and what it says has to be true.

    The route map had no `health` entry while the engine and the browser worker
    both published one, so a probe walking the stack's services on one path list
    got `404` from Django on every poll: a log line claiming the gateway was down
    while the gateway was the process answering the request. The route is the
    defect, so the route is what these tests pin first.

    The rest pins the part that is easy to get wrong in the other direction. A
    liveness endpoint that reports `ok: true` and folds every dependency into it
    is worse than no endpoint, because it converts an outage into a green light.
    So the body has to separate the gateway from the services behind it, and a
    service that does not answer has to be named as down rather than omitted.
    """

    def test_the_route_exists_and_answers_json(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.get("/health")
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        payload = response.json()
        self.assertTrue(payload["ok"])
        # The gateway answering is not the interesting half; identifying which
        # service answered is what makes the endpoint usable by a caller that
        # cannot tell the four apart from the port alone.
        self.assertEqual(payload["service"], "web")

    def test_it_is_the_only_non_api_route_the_monitoring_can_use(self) -> None:
        # Every other route the browser talks to lives under `/api/`. A monitor
        # probing a fixed service path list would otherwise have to know that
        # Django answers `/` and the other two answer `/health`.
        from django.urls import resolve

        self.assertEqual(resolve("/health").view_name, "health")

    def test_a_reachable_stack_reports_each_service_up(self) -> None:
        response = self._probe(engine=200, worker=200)
        payload = response.json()
        self.assertTrue(payload["database"]["ok"])
        self.assertIsNone(payload["database"]["error"])
        self.assertTrue(payload["services"]["engine"]["ok"])
        self.assertEqual(payload["services"]["engine"]["status"], 200)
        self.assertTrue(payload["services"]["browser_worker"]["ok"])
        self.assertEqual(payload["services"]["browser_worker"]["status"], 200)

    def test_a_dead_engine_is_named_and_does_not_flip_the_status_code(self) -> None:
        # The gateway is genuinely alive here — it is answering this request — so
        # the HTTP status stays 200 and the dead service is reported in the body.
        # Reporting 5xx here would be a lie in the other direction: it would tell
        # a supervisor to restart the one process that is working.
        payload = self._probe(engine=None, worker=200).json()
        engine = payload["services"]["engine"]
        self.assertFalse(engine["ok"])
        self.assertIsNone(engine["status"])
        self.assertIn("unavailable", engine["error"])
        self.assertTrue(payload["services"]["browser_worker"]["ok"])

    def test_a_dead_browser_worker_is_named(self) -> None:
        payload = self._probe(engine=200, worker=502).json()
        worker = payload["services"]["browser_worker"]
        self.assertFalse(worker["ok"])
        self.assertEqual(worker["status"], 502)

    def test_the_browser_catalogue_and_its_reasons_are_passed_through(self) -> None:
        # The worker's `/health` is the only place a runtime's availability is
        # measured, and it names a reason per runtime. An endpoint that dropped
        # that would make the operator make a second request to learn which
        # browsers this installation can actually start.
        payload = self._probe(
            engine=200,
            worker=200,
            worker_body={
                "browsers": ["firefox", "camoufox"],
                "unavailable": {"chromium": "not downloaded at /cache/chromium"},
            },
        ).json()
        worker = payload["services"]["browser_worker"]
        self.assertEqual(worker["browsers"], ["firefox", "camoufox"])
        self.assertEqual(
            worker["unavailable"], {"chromium": "not downloaded at /cache/chromium"}
        )

    def test_an_unreachable_database_is_reported_rather_than_hidden(self) -> None:
        with patch.object(views.connection, "cursor", side_effect=OperationalError("cluster gone")):
            payload = self._probe(engine=200, worker=200).json()
        self.assertFalse(payload["database"]["ok"])
        self.assertIn("cluster gone", payload["database"]["error"])
        # The gateway itself still answers: a database outage is not a gateway
        # outage, and restarting the web process would not fix it.
        self.assertTrue(payload["ok"])

    def test_a_service_that_is_not_listening_is_not_a_transport_crash(self) -> None:
        # `URLError` is the ordinary shape of "nothing is listening". Left
        # uncaught it would turn a stopped engine into a 500 traceback on the
        # endpoint whose entire job is to say that engine is stopped.
        payload = self._probe(engine=URLError("connection refused"), worker=200).json()
        self.assertFalse(payload["services"]["engine"]["ok"])

    def test_a_non_json_health_body_is_still_a_reachable_service(self) -> None:
        # A 200 with an unexpected body means the service is up and misbehaving.
        # Reporting that as unreachable would send an operator to restart a
        # process that is answering.
        payload = self._probe(engine=200, worker=200, engine_body=b"<html>hi</html>").json()
        engine = payload["services"]["engine"]
        self.assertTrue(engine["ok"])
        self.assertEqual(engine["error"], "health response is not JSON")

    def test_a_write_method_is_refused(self) -> None:
        # Health is read-only and unauthenticated, like the other two services',
        # so it must not answer anything that could change state.
        self.assertEqual(self.client.post("/health").status_code, 405)

    def _probe(self, engine, worker, engine_body=None, worker_body=None) -> None:
        """Answer `/health` with the two internal services pinned.

        The database is left real on purpose: it is reachable in the test runner,
        and a test that mocked it too would not tell whether the view reads it at
        all.
        """

        def engine_urlopen(request, timeout=None):
            if isinstance(engine, Exception):
                raise engine
            if isinstance(engine, int) and engine != 200:
                raise HTTPError(request.full_url, engine, "boom", {}, None)
            body = engine_body if engine_body is not None else b'{"ok":true}'
            return _FakeUrlopenResponse(engine if isinstance(engine, int) else 200, body)

        def worker_call(path):
            if isinstance(worker, Exception):
                return 502, {"error": str(worker)}
            if worker != 200:
                return worker, {"error": "worker health check failed"}
            return 200, worker_body or {"browsers": ["firefox"], "unavailable": {}}

        with patch.object(views, "urlopen", side_effect=engine_urlopen), patch.object(
            views, "call_browser_worker_get", side_effect=worker_call
        ):
            return self.client.get("/health")


class _FakeUrlopenResponse:
    """The minimum `urlopen` result the health probe reads."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, body: bytes) -> None:
        self.status = status
        self._body = body

    def read(self) -> bytes:
        return self._body

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_exc) -> bool:
        return False

def _probe_internal_service(base_url, path):
    """GET a service's `/health` with a short deadline.

    Returns `(status, payload, decoded)`. The third value says whether the body
    was the JSON this endpoint was written to read, and it is not decoration: a
    service answering `200` with an HTML error page is reachable but is not
    reporting health, and folding the two into one boolean would report a
    misconfigured service as healthy — the same failure this view exists to
    remove, one level up.

    A separate helper rather than a call to `call_engine_get`, because that one
    carries the route generation and the general 120-second engine timeout: both
    are wrong for a liveness probe. The generation would make a health answer
    depend on which route generation the browser last applied, and the deadline
    would let one wedged engine hold a health request open for two minutes — on
    an endpoint that is polled every few seconds.
    """
    try:
        request = Request(f"{base_url}{path}", headers=internal_service_headers(), method="GET")
        with urlopen(request, timeout=HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT) as response:
            body = response.read()
            status = response.status
        try:
            return status, json.loads(body), True
        except ValueError:
            # Reachable, answering something other than health. The status is
            # kept as it arrived and the reason is named, so the caller sees a
            # live service with a wrong answer rather than a dead one.
            return status, {"error": "health response is not JSON"}, False
    except HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, {"error": error.read().decode(errors="replace")[:200]}, False
    except (URLError, TimeoutError, RemoteDisconnected, ConnectionError, socket.timeout) as error:
        return None, {"error": f"unavailable: {getattr(error, 'reason', error)}"}, False

"""Firefox: повна папка `http` має завершитися, а не зависнути.

Сценарій робить те, що робить оператор: відкриває UI у Firefox, обирає вкладку
Scanner → Nuclei, вказує реальну теку, завантажує ПОВНУ папку `http` через
`webkitdirectory` і тисне Run. Далі чекає термінального стану — і читає його з
інтерфейсу, а не з API: `Completed` / `Cancelled` / `Failed`.

Очікувані числа передаються аргументом, тому прогон їх утверджує, а не
описує: якщо задано --min-rows, перевірка падає, коли рядків менше.

Прогін довший за сесію агента, тому запускається через setsid, а PID
записується — і гаситься за цим PID у фіналі.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys
import time

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"


def read_text(page, selector):
    node = page.query_selector(selector)
    if node is None:
        return ""
    try:
        return node.inner_text().strip()
    except Exception:
        return ""


def panel(page):
    return (
        read_text(page, "#scanner-progress-phase"),
        read_text(page, "#scanner-progress-stats"),
        read_text(page, "#scanner-status"),
    )


def open_scanner(page):
    page.click('nav [data-tab="scanner"]')
    page.wait_for_timeout(400)
    page.click("#scanner-view-nuclei")
    page.wait_for_timeout(300)


def report(page):
    phase, stats, status = panel(page)
    rows = len(page.query_selector_all("#scanner-tpl-body tr"))
    files_done = rows
    return {
        "phase": phase,
        "stats": " | ".join(stats.split("\n"))[:160],
        "status": status[:80],
        "rows": rows,
        "files_done": files_done,
    }


TERMINAL = ("completed", "cancelled", "failed", "complete", "cancel", "fail")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--corpus", default="/home/kali/Desktop/DevBackUp-vecher07101/nuclei-templates/http")
    parser.add_argument("--target", default="https://yandex.ru")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=3000, help="seconds to wait for a terminal state")
    parser.add_argument("--min-rows", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--poll", type=int, default=15)
    parser.add_argument("--out", default="/tmp/opencode/http-full-run.json")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    started = time.time()
    errors = []
    with sync_playwright() as play:
        browser = play.firefox.launch(headless=True)
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1356, "height": 652})
        page.on("console", lambda m: errors.append(f"[{m.type}] {m.text}") if m.type == "error" else None)
        page.on("pageerror", lambda e: errors.append(f"[pageerror] {e}"))

        page.goto(BASE + "/", wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=90_000)
        open_scanner(page)
        page.fill("#scanner-url", args.target)

        upload_started = time.time()
        page.set_input_files("#scanner-yaml-dir", args.corpus)
        # The upload loop reports per chunk; give it room and watch the panel
        # rather than sleeping blind.
        upload_done = None
        while time.time() - upload_started < 600:
            page.wait_for_timeout(5000)
            phase, stats, _ = panel(page)
            print(f"  upload t={int(time.time() - upload_started):3d}s phase={phase[:14]!r} {stats.splitlines()[:1]}", flush=True)
            if "Uploading" not in phase and ("Preparing" in phase or "Ready" in phase or "Готов" in phase):
                upload_done = time.time()
                break
        upload_seconds = round((upload_done or time.time()) - upload_started, 1)
        print(f"upload: {upload_seconds}s", flush=True)

        page.click("#scanner-templates-run")
        run_started = time.time()
        job_id = None
        deadline = run_started + args.timeout
        last = None
        while time.time() < deadline:
            page.wait_for_timeout(args.poll * 1000)
            state = report(page)
            job_id = job_id or page.evaluate("() => localStorage.getItem('scanner-active-nuclei-job')")
            elapsed = int(time.time() - run_started)
            print(
                f"t={elapsed:5d}s phase={state['phase'][:16]!r} rows={state['rows']:5d} {state['stats'][:90]}",
                flush=True,
            )
            last = state
            if any(token in state["phase"].lower() for token in TERMINAL):
                break

        final = report(page)
        run_seconds = round(time.time() - run_started, 1)
        page.screenshot(path="/tmp/opencode/http-full-run.png", full_page=False)

        result = {
            "corpus": args.corpus,
            "target": args.target,
            "upload_seconds": upload_seconds,
            "run_seconds": run_seconds,
            "job_id": job_id,
            "final": final,
            "terminal": any(t in final["phase"].lower() for t in TERMINAL),
            "console_errors": errors[-10:],
            "screenshot": "/tmp/opencode/http-full-run.png",
        }
        with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(result, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

        # A scan left running when the harness stops is our own mess, so cancel
        # it here rather than leaving a binary running for an hour.
        if not result["terminal"]:
            cancel = page.query_selector("#scanner-progress-cancel")
            if cancel and cancel.is_visible():
                cancel.click()
                page.wait_for_timeout(6000)
                print("cancelled:", report(page)["phase"], flush=True)

        print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
        browser.close()

    if args.min_rows and result["final"]["rows"] < args.min_rows:
        print(f"FAIL: {result['final']['rows']} rows < --min-rows {args.min_rows}")
        return 1
    if not result["terminal"]:
        print("FAIL: no terminal state reached")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Повна папка `http` через Firefox: чи завершується прогін.

Робить те, що робить оператор: відкриває UI, обирає Scanner → Nuclei, вводить

термінального стану, читаючи його з інтерфейсу.

Дві поправки проти попередніх версій, обидві через вимірювання, не через
припущення:

* панель `Uploading` — це фаза **ще до** запуску, тому вихід із циклу на ній
  ніколи не доходив до Run і не запускав скан;
* `setScanProgress` всередині циклу пише стан **перед** кожним чанком, тому
  останнє написане значення описує стан перед останнім чанком — читати треба
  після завершення стейджингу, а не під час нього.

Очікувані числа передаються аргументом: прогон їх утверджує, а не описує.
"""

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
import time

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
DIGITS = re.compile(r"(\d[\d\s.,]*)")
# Anything that is not an in-progress phase. The panel has to reach one of these
# before the harness stops waiting.
DONE_TOKENS = ("completed", "cancelled", "failed", "complete", "cancel", "fail", "завершено", "скасовано")
BUSY_TOKENS = ("scanning", "queued", "uploading", "preparing", "loading", "скан", "підготов")


def read_text(page, selector):
    node = page.query_selector(selector)
    if node is None:
        return ""
    try:
        return node.inner_text().strip()
    except Exception:
        return ""


def digits(text):
    return [int(n.replace(" ", "").replace(",", "").replace(".", "")) for n in DIGITS.findall(text or "")]


def open_scanner(page):
    page.click('nav [data-tab="scanner"]')
    page.wait_for_timeout(400)
    page.click("#scanner-view-nuclei")
    page.wait_for_timeout(300)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--corpus", default="/home/kali/Desktop/DevBackUp-vecher07101/nuclei-templates/http")
    parser.add_argument("--target", default="https://yandex.ru")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=5400)
    parser.add_argument("--poll", type=int, default=20)
    parser.add_argument("--min-files", type=int, default=11000)
    parser.add_argument("--min-rows", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--out", default="/tmp/opencode/http-full-run2.json")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    errors = []
    result = {}
    with sync_playwright() as play:
        browser = play.firefox.launch(headless=True)
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1356, "height": 652})
        page.on("console", lambda m: errors.append(f"[{m.type}] {m.text}"[:180]) if m.type == "error" else None)
        page.on("pageerror", lambda e: errors.append(f"[pageerror] {e}"[:180]))

        page.goto(BASE + "/", wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=90_000)
        open_scanner(page)
        page.fill("#scanner-url", args.target)
        page.set_input_files("#scanner-yaml-dir", args.corpus)

        # Phase 1 — the browser reads the folder locally. The status wording is
        # `done / total` while reading and a single total once it is finished, so
        # both are read as digits and the workspace language cannot break it.
        read_started = time.time()
        total_files = 0
        while time.time() - read_started < 900:
            page.wait_for_timeout(3000)
            status = read_text(page, "#scanner-status")
            numbers = digits(status)
            total_files = numbers[-1] if numbers else 0
            print(f"  read t={int(time.time() - read_started):3d}s status={status[:56]!r}", flush=True)
            if total_files >= args.min_files and len(numbers) == 1:
                break
        read_seconds = round(time.time() - read_started, 1)
        print(f"read: {read_seconds}s, {total_files} files", flush=True)
        if total_files < args.min_files:
            result = {"stage": "read", "total_files": total_files, "read_seconds": read_seconds}
            print(f"FAIL: read {total_files} files, expected >= {args.min_files}")
            browser.close()
            return 1

        # Phase 2 — Run. Staging and job start both happen here; `Uploading` is
        # still "not started yet", so it must not end the wait.
        page.click("#scanner-templates-run")
        run_started = time.time()
        job_id = None
        phase = ""
        while time.time() - run_started < args.timeout:
            page.wait_for_timeout(args.poll * 1000)
            phase = read_text(page, "#scanner-progress-phase")
            stats = read_text(page, "#scanner-progress-stats")
            status = read_text(page, "#scanner-status")
            job_id = job_id or page.evaluate("() => localStorage.getItem('scanner-active-nuclei-job')")
            rows = len(page.query_selector_all("#scanner-tpl-body tr"))
            elapsed = int(time.time() - run_started)
            print(
                f"t={elapsed:5d}s phase={phase[:18]!r} rows={rows:6d} job={job_id} "
                f"stats={' | '.join(stats.split(chr(10)))[:70]} status={status[:40]!r}",
                flush=True,
            )
            low = phase.lower()
            if any(token in low for token in DONE_TOKENS) and not any(b in low for b in BUSY_TOKENS):
                break

        final_phase = read_text(page, "#scanner-progress-phase")
        final_stats = read_text(page, "#scanner-progress-stats")
        rows = len(page.query_selector_all("#scanner-tpl-body tr"))
        run_seconds = round(time.time() - run_started, 1)
        page.screenshot(path="/tmp/opencode/http-full-run2.png")

        terminal = any(t in final_phase.lower() for t in DONE_TOKENS) and not any(
            b in final_phase.lower() for b in BUSY_TOKENS
        )

        # The engine is asked directly what it thinks, so a panel that claims a
        # state is checked against the job rather than trusted.
        engine_state = None
        if job_id:
            try:
                engine_state = page.request.get(f"{BASE}/api/scanner/nuclei/jobs/{job_id}").json()
            except Exception as error:
                engine_state = {"error": str(error)}

        result = {
            "corpus": args.corpus,
            "target": args.target,
            "total_files": total_files,
            "read_seconds": read_seconds,
            "run_seconds": run_seconds,
            "job_id": job_id,
            "final_phase": final_phase,
            "final_stats": " | ".join(final_stats.split("\n")),
            "rows": rows,
            "terminal": terminal,
            "engine_state": engine_state,
            "console_errors": errors[-8:],
            "screenshot": "/tmp/opencode/http-full-run2.png",
        }

        if not terminal:
            cancel = page.query_selector("#scanner-progress-cancel")
            if cancel and cancel.is_visible():
                cancel.click()
                page.wait_for_timeout(6000)
                print("cancelled ->", read_text(page, "#scanner-progress-phase"), flush=True)

        with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(result, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
        print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)[:2500])
        browser.close()

    if not result["terminal"]:
        print("FAIL: no terminal state reached")
        return 1
    if args.min_rows and result["rows"] < args.min_rows:
        print(f"FAIL: {result['rows']} rows < --min-rows {args.min_rows}")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

+	//
+	// `hijackBoundedConns` is what keeps a MITM tunnel from living forever, and it
+	// has to sit HERE rather than on the `http.Server`: `HandleConnect(AlwaysMitm)`
+	// resolves to goproxy's `ConnectMitm`, and that path calls `Hijack()`
+	// (`https.go:271`). A hijacked connection leaves the server's own machinery
+	// immediately, so `ReadHeaderTimeout`, `IdleTimeout` and `WriteTimeout` stop
+	// applying to it — the engine API sets all three (`main.go:678`) and none of
+	// them would ever reach a tunnel. After the 200 confirmation goproxy only
+	// `io.Copy`s between the two sockets, with no deadline on either.

+	// Measured on the full `http` corpus through this proxy, against
+	// `https://yandex.ru`: 82 tunnels ESTAB with the request counter frozen at
+	// 6395/20675 and nuclei down to a single thread at 0% CPU, while the same
+	// corpus in a terminal finished in 189 s. Nothing closed those 82 connections:
+	// each one waited for the other side forever.
 	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
-		proxy.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+		proxy.ServeHTTP(&hijackBoundedResponseWriter{ResponseWriter: w}, r)
 	})
 }
 
+// MITMIdleTimeout bounds how long a hijacked tunnel may carry no bytes at all.
+//
+// It is an idle bound, not a lifetime: every read or write that actually moves
+// data resets it, so a long scan over one connection is untouched. What it
+// removes is the connection that stopped talking and stayed counted — one
+// socket, one goroutine each way, and one of the analyzer's own concurrency
+// slots held open for the rest of the run.
+//
+// Overridable from the environment like every other deadline in the engine, and
+// it bounds nothing the operator asked for: set it to 0 to keep the previous
+// behaviour of never expiring an idle tunnel.
+var MITMIdleTimeout = func() time.Duration {
+	if seconds, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("RR_MITM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC")), 64); err == nil && seconds > 0 {
+		return time.Duration(seconds * float64(time.Second))
+	}
+	return 90 * time.Second
+}()
+
+// deadlineConn applies MITMIdleTimeout to every read and write on a hijacked
+// connection.
+//
+// The deadline is set before each operation and cleared after it succeeds, so
+// the bound is on idleness rather than on total time. A connection transferring
+// data continuously — which is what a scan through this proxy does — never sees
+// it fire.
+type deadlineConn struct {
+	net.Conn
+	idle time.Duration
+}
+
+// Read bounds one read by the idle timeout and lifts the deadline afterwards.
+func (c *deadlineConn) Read(b []byte) (int, error) {
+	if c.idle > 0 {
+		_ = c.Conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(c.idle))
+	}
+	n, err := c.Conn.Read(b)
+	if n > 0 || err == nil {
+		_ = c.Conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Time{})
+	}
+	return n, err
+}
+
+// Write bounds one write the same way. The error is passed through untouched:
+// a partial write must not be reported as success, and the caller decides what
+// a deadline means for its own exchange.
+func (c *deadlineConn) Write(b []byte) (int, error) {
+	if c.idle > 0 {
+		_ = c.Conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(c.idle))
+	}
+	n, err := c.Conn.Write(b)
+	if n > 0 || err == nil {
+		_ = c.Conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Time{})
+	}
+	return n, err
+}
+
+// hijackBoundedResponseWriter hands goproxy a connection that expires when it
+// goes idle.
+//
+// goproxy needs `http.Hijacker` and type-asserts for it, so the wrapper has to
+// implement the interface rather than just wrap it. The other optional
+// interfaces goproxy looks for are preserved by delegation, because dropping one
+// would silently change the path goproxy takes.
+type hijackBoundedResponseWriter struct {
+	http.ResponseWriter
+}
+
+// Hijack is the whole point: the connection goproxy takes over from here is
+// wrapped once, and every later read and write on it is bounded.
+func (w *hijackBoundedResponseWriter) Hijack() (net.Conn, *bufio.ReadWriter, error) {
+	hijacker, ok := w.ResponseWriter.(http.Hijacker)
+	if !ok {
+		// Reporting this rather than pretending: goproxy turns a missing
+		// Hijacker into an HTTP/2-only path, and the operator would see requests
+		// fail without being told why.
+		return nil, nil, errNoHijacker
+	}
+	conn, buffered, err := hijacker.Hijack()
+	if err != nil {
+		return conn, buffered, err
+	}
+	if MITMIdleTimeout > 0 {
+		conn = &deadlineConn{Conn: conn, idle: MITMIdleTimeout}
+	}
+	return conn, buffered, nil
+}
+
+// Flush keeps the streaming path available to goproxy; without it a wrapped
+// response writer that goproxy can flush through would turn every flush into a
+// no-op and buffer the whole exchange.
+func (w *hijackBoundedResponseWriter) Flush() {
+	if flusher, ok := w.ResponseWriter.(http.Flusher); ok {
+		flusher.Flush()
+	}
+}

+var errNoHijacker = errors.New("passive proxy: response writer does not support hijacking")

"""Чи закриває проксі MITM-тунель, який перестав передавати дані.

Відкриває CONNECT, читає відповідь 200, потім мовчить і чекає, коли сервер
закриє з'єднання саме з боку сервера. Це те, що не робив жоден таймаут.
"""
import socket, sys, time

PROXY = ("127.0.0.1", 8080)
WAIT = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 20.0

s = socket.create_connection(PROXY, timeout=10)
s.sendall(b"CONNECT yandex.ru:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: yandex.ru:443\r\n\r\n")
s.settimeout(WAIT)
data = b""
t0 = time.time()
try:
    while b"\r\n\r\n" not in data and time.time() - t0 < WAIT:
        chunk = s.recv(4096)
        if not chunk:
            print(f"закрито одразу після CONNECT через {time.time()-t0:.1f}s")
            sys.exit(0)
        data += chunk
except socket.timeout:
    print(f"тунель живий після {WAIT:.0f}s мовчання — НЕ закрито")
    sys.exit(1)
print("CONNECT:", data.split(b"\r\n")[0].decode(errors="replace"))
# Тепер мовчимо і чекаємо, коли сервер закриє сам.
t0 = time.time()
try:
    while True:
        chunk = s.recv(4096)
        if not chunk:
            print(f"сервер закрив тунель через {time.time()-t0:.1f}s мовчання")
            sys.exit(0)
except socket.timeout:
    print(f"сервер НЕ закрив тунель за {WAIT:.0f}s — idle-межа не діє")
    sys.exit(1)

 Если хотя бы один обязательный пункт не выполнен:

```
COMPLIANCE: FAIL
```

 Агент НЕ ИМЕЕТ ПРАВА сообщать об успешном завершении.

---

 # 13 ПРИНЦИП «ОСТАНОВИТЬСЯ, А НЕ НАРУШИТЬ»

Если агент не может одновременно выполнить задачу и соблюдать инструкции, он ОБЯЗАН
остановиться.

 Приоритет:

```
ОСТАНОВИТЬСЯ И СООБЩИТЬ О ПРОБЛЕМЕ
```

 вместо:

```
ПРИДУМАТЬ ОБХОДНОЙ ПУТЬ И НАРУШИТЬ ИНСТРУКЦИИ
```

 Запрещено:

 - угадывать;
- самостоятельно создавать исключения;
- игнорировать ограничение;
- скрывать нарушение;
- продолжать работу после обнаружения конфликта.

---

 # 14 АГЕНТ НЕ МОЖЕТ СОЗДАВАТЬ ИСКЛЮЧЕНИЯ ДЛЯ СЕБЯ

 Следующие аргументы НЕ дают агенту разрешения нарушить правила:

 - «Это безопасное изменение».
- «Это всего одна строка».
- «Это очевидно».
- «Это необходимо».
- «Это никак не повлияет».
- «Тест можно не запускать».
- «Это незначительное изменение».
- «Я просто немного улучшу код».
- «Пользователь наверняка имел это в виду».

Исключение действительно только тогда, когда оно явно разрешено применимыми инструкциями
или пользователем.

---

 # 15 ЗАЩИТА ОТ САМОПРОИЗВОЛЬНОЙ СМЕНЫ СТРАТЕГИИ

 После начала выполнения агент НЕ ДОЛЖЕН самостоятельно менять стратегию реализации.

 Если выбранный подход оказался невозможным:

```
СТОП
↓
ОБЪЯСНИТЬ ПРОБЛЕМУ
↓
ОБНОВИТЬ ПЛАН
↓
ЗАФИКСИРОВАТЬ ИЗМЕНЕНИЕ
↓
ПРОДОЛЖИТЬ
```

Нельзя незаметно перейти на другой подход и продолжить работу так, будто план не
изменился.

---

 # 16 ФИНАЛЬНЫЙ ОТЧЁТ

 После выполнения задачи агент ОБЯЗАН предоставить:

```
ЗАДАЧА:
...

ПЛАН:
...

ВЫПОЛНЕННЫЕ ИЗМЕНЕНИЯ:
- ...

ПРОВЕРКИ:
- ...

ИЗМЕНЁННЫЕ ФАЙЛЫ:
- ...

COMPLIANCE:
PASS / FAIL

ИЗМЕНЕНИЯ ВНЕ ПЛАНА:
НЕТ / <описание>

ПРОБЛЕМЫ:
...
```

 `COMPLIANCE: PASS` разрешено указывать ТОЛЬКО после успешного прохождения всех обязательных проверок.

 Если хотя бы одно обязательное требование нарушено:

```
COMPLIANCE: FAIL
```

---

 # 17 КРИТЕРИЙ ЗАВЕРШЕНИЯ

 Задача считается выполненной ТОЛЬКО если одновременно выполнены все условия:

```
РЕЗУЛЬТАТ СООТВЕТСТВУЕТ ЗАПРОСУ
            +
ПЛАН ВЫПОЛНЕН
            +
AGENTS.md СОБЛЮДЁН
            +
ЗАПРЕЩЁННЫЕ ФАЙЛЫ НЕ ИЗМЕНЕНЫ
            +
НЕСАНКЦИОНИРОВАННЫХ ИЗМЕНЕНИЙ НЕТ
            +
ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНЫЕ ПРОВЕРКИ ПРОЙДЕНЫ
            +
ФИНАЛЬНЫЙ DIFF ПРОВЕРЕН
            +
COMPLIANCE-CHECK = PASS
```

Технически работающий код, который нарушает этот контракт, считается **НЕВЫПОЛНЕННОЙ
ЗАДАЧЕЙ**.

 Главная цель агента:

 > **Не просто сделать рабочий код, а сделать именно то, что было запланировано, строго
 > в рамках инструкций, с доказуемым соблюдением всех ограничений.**

 Если хочешь **реально жёсткий enforcement**, а не только промпт, следующий шаг — добавить к этому `AGENTS.md` механизм, который автоматически сравнивает `git diff` с планом и **роняет задачу/CI при изменении запрещённого файла или появлении изменений вне плана**.

     никакого CDN, никакого внешнего шрифта. OSINT Entity Graph —
     local native SVG, а не сторонняя библиотека. Поэтому любая новая
     browser-фича добавляется тем же способом: ручной CSS в общем
     `<style>` и ручной JS в общем инлайн-блоке, с `data-i18n` для
     строк.
   - **Сторонние библиотеки разрешены (решение владельца 2026-09-27).**
     `React Flow`, `Cytoscape.js` и `Monaco Editor` — разрешённый стек, а не

     Обязательные условия для каждой: локально вендоренный бандл (никакого
     CDN), фиксированная версия, и ни одна не имеет права ломать инварианты
     раскладки, источник правды для токенов, полноту i18n или контракт
     экспорта. Точный перечень рисков по
     каждой библиотеке — в разделе «Технический стек и архитектура» выше.
     Полный React-rewrite страницы — по-прежнему запрещён без прямого запроса
     владельца.

2. **High-Speed Attack & Network Engine (`engine/`):**
   - **Language:** Go (Golang)[cite: 1].
   -  **Responsibilities:** асинхронная обработка сырых TCP/TLS сокетов, HTTP/1.1 и

### Основные инженерные и архитектурные принципы

1. **Principle of Non-Blocking Operations:**
   - Request-Rider — это инструмент исследователя[cite: 1]. Логика `Scope` (In-Scope / Out-of-Scope) запрещена в данном проекте!

2. **Single Source of Truth (Project Hub):**
   - Все сущности (перехваченный трафик, найденные поддомены OSINT, уязвимости Findings, реестр секретов ProjectSecret, карты эндпоинтов ProjectEndpoint, Intruder , Scanner (Nuclei and CMS ) автоматически привязываются к `active_project_id`[cite: 1].

3. **No Hallucinations & Production-Ready Code:**
   - Запрещено использовать заглушки вида `// TODO: implement later` или сокращать код в ключевых местах.
   - Весь сгенерированный код должен быть сразу готов к выполнению, обрабатывать исключения (Error Handling) и не ломать имеющиеся функции в проекте (`web/lab/tests.py`)[cite: 1].

4. **Database Integrity:**
   - Любые изменения в моделях Django (`web/lab/models.py`) должны сопровождаться новыми корректными файлами миграций (`python manage.py makemigrations`)[cite: 1].

5.   Автоматизированное сканирование а так же использование всех инстурментов на внешних

### Execution Workflow for AI Agent

При получении задачи всегда соблюдай 4-этапный цикл:

1. **Context Check:** проанализируй имеющуюся кодовую базу, файлы миграций и модуль `runtime_limits.py` перед внесением изменений[cite: 1]. Модуль фиксирует отсутствие **скрытых** caps на пользовательские значения; это не запрещает явных технических пределов, разрешённых разделом «Технические пределы выполнения разрешены»[cite: 1].
2. **Architecture Plan:** сформулируй короткий пошаговый план изменений с точным указанием задействованных файлов (`engine/`, `web/lab/`, `web/templates/`).
3.   **Clean Implementation:** напиши чистый, оптимизированный код с соблюдением
   стандартов PEP8 (Python) и Go Code Review (Go).
4.   **Verification & Tests:** убедись, что написанный код обратно совместим с другими
   модулями и включает нужные юнит-тесты или обёртки.
5.   **Делать тотько то-что попросили** - а если хочешь что то поменять нужно обьясняить
   зачем это нужно и обгрунтовать данное решение
6. **Агентная сессия** — если во время работы оператор добавляет поправку,
   замечание или баг, оно **записывается в файл сессии** и исправляется **по
   порядку**. Запрещено бросать недоделанную работу и начинать новую. У каждой
   сессии агента свой файл. Полное правило и разграничение с git —
   `Управление задачами и сессиями` в Части VII.
7. **Спрашивай, а не угадывай.** Это не тактическая вежливость, а условие, без
   которого остальные пункты не работают. **Не понял задачу или тебе прямо не
   сказали, что делать — задай вопрос и остановись на нём.** Правило владельца
   2026-09-28, принято после реального случая: агент услышал «после работы
   браузеры не должны висеть», **решил сам**, что правится продукт, полез
   переписывать `browser-worker/worker.py` — а владелец просил только текст
   правила в `AGENTS.md`. Потеряно время, изменён не тот слой, и агент полез
   «чинить» файл с чужой незакоммиченной работой, которую не имеет права
   коммитить.

   Что это значит на практике:

   - **Два разных прочитания одного слова — это вопрос, а не выбор.** «Не
     висят» может означать «поведение продукта» или «поведение агента». Это
     разные задачи в разных файлах, и угадать нельзя.
   - **Задача не про тот слой, который ты нашёл первой — спроси.** Наличие
     убедительного кода рядом не делает его твоей целью.
   - **Ничего не начинай «на всякий случай».** Правка, тест, стенд или
     коммит, о которых не просили, — это не инициатива, это самовольность.
   - **Один вопрос — конкретный.** Не «как вам лучше?», а «правило в
     `AGENTS.md` или правка в `worker.py`?».

   Чего правило **не** требует: не спрашивать о каждом шаге, если задача ясна,
   и не задавать вопрос, ответ на который не меняет результат (см.
   `Ключевые договорённости`). Граница простая: **ясная задача — делай,
   неясная — спрашивай.** Цена ошибки несимметрична: лишний вопрос стоит одного
   сообщения, а лишняя правка чужого слоя — отката в чужой сессии.

### Короткий контекст

RequestRider —  QA-инструмент для ручного анализа HTTP и разрешённого
тестирования. Текущий стек:

```text
Browser :8000
    -> Django web gateway + PostgreSQL History
    -> Go engine :8081
         -> outbound request execution
         -> Intruder generation/execution
         -> Target site-map crawling
         -> passive MITM proxy :8080
```

Для smoke-тестов Intruder используется внешняя разрешённая цель,
переданная явно через конфигурацию запуска.

#### Запрещено на уровне проекта
-  Запрещено хардкодить ограничения типа limit/ scope / allowlist / denylist /
  private-target blocking в выполнении инструментов и workflow.

-  Проект является организационным workspace и knowledge base, а не файрволом или policy
  engine;

-  Запрещено встраивать пользовательские “scope gate”, “authorized scope”, “out of
  scope” блокеры в UI/конфигурацию

-  Агент не пишет policy/allowlist/denylist/scope-blocking код ни при каких условиях и
  обстоятельствах: никаких самостоятельных ограничений выполнения, никаких скрытых
  проверок зон/доменов/IP в коде. Рамки разрешённого существуют лишь как текст
  договорённости , а не как код.

#### Технические пределы выполнения разрешены

> Решение владельца 2026-09-27. Запрет выше касается **политик в отношении целей**,
> а не инженерной надёжности. Путаница этих двух вещей и блокировала четыре
> пункта плана (2.1, 2.3, 3.2, 5.1) без какой-либо реальной основы.

**Разрешено и должно быть реализовано:**

- управляемая конкурентность: worker pool, количество одновременных сетевых соединений,
семафоры для brute-force/fuzz/парсинга; Так чтобы это не ограничевало пользователя - это
сделанно чтобы мертвые воркеры соединения и прочее очищались!
 
- явные таймауты внешних запросов: dial/connect, TLS handshake, header, total 
  response deadline; `context.WithTimeout` в каждой функции, которая делает
  внешний запрос; Но не ставали проблемой из за слишком большого или маленького таймаут 

- navigation timeout в браузерном воркере (`page.goto(..., timeout=...)`);

- очереди и потребительские квоты брокера, retry/backoff ceilings, таймауты
  на poll и shutdown;
  
- песочница для пользовательского кода: лимит инструкций, время выполнения, размер
  памяти и доступных host capabilities;
  
- кэш-пределы, размер очереди, размер батча для чтения больших ответов.

**Обязательное условие: предел не должен мешать нормальной работе приложения.**

1. Предел **не уменьшает** возможностей инструмента: любая цель, любой объём,
   любая глубина, любой размер словаря остаются доступными.
   Ограничение ресурсов ≠ ограничение разведки.
2. Пользователь перекрывает предел **явным вводом**, и тогда он не действует.
3. Применение предела **видно**: отображается в UI, строке состояния или telemetry.
Скрытый предел, которого не видно, нарушает это правило так же, как cap. Или на который
пользовватель явно не может повляить и испрвить или изменить!
4. Предел защищает от **зависания и утечки ресурсов** (зависшая горутина, мёртвый
   сокет, бесконечный цикл, вытеснение памяти), а не от слишком большой
   работы.
5. Значения, заданные пользователем, передаются в выполнение **без верхнего
   предела**. Если предел существует, он приходит либо из явного поля запроса, либо из
   задокументированного default — и в обоих случаях виден.

**Код-контракт.** Запрещён *скрытый* cap, который не читается из
конфигурации. Правильная форма — `timeout`/`iterations`/`concurrency` в явном
поле с default-ом и видимым состоянием; неправильная — константа в теле цикла, которая
обрывает результат без уведомления.
